summary: Palmo Kyi is a scholar in Tibetology who studied under supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012) and teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University from around 1971 to 1976.

Panahaduwe Yasassi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was Professor in Buddhist Civilization at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura in 2020 and a Venerable Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He served as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and held various teaching and legal posts.

Pankaj Tandon specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at St. Stephen's College, Delhi School of Economics, and Harvard University under mentor Tom Mallon-McCorgray, he became an Associate Professor at Boston University in 1978.

Paolo Daffinà (d. 2009) was a scholar of Central Asian studies, sinology, and history. He earned his Ph.D. at Sapienza University of Rome in 1953 under Giuseppe Tucci, Luciano Petech, and Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, later serving as Sapienza's director (1973–1982).

Paolo Emilio Pavolini (1864–1942) was an Italian Indologist and linguist. He studied at Pisa and Berlin under Emilio Teza, Albrecht Weber, and Richard Pischel, and served as Professore ordinario at the University of Florence from 1895 to 1935.

Paolo Visigalli is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Padua, and the University of Cambridge (~2011–2015), he held posts at NYU Shanghai (~2017–2021) and Shanghai Normal University (~2021).

Paramahansa Yogananda (1893–1952) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Scottish Church College (~1910–1912), the Senate of Serampore College (~1913–1915), and the University of Calcutta (~1913–1915).

Paramita Paul specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Leiden University in 2009 and has served as a Lecturer at Amsterdam University College and Chief Editor at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya (1891–1978) studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Louis de La Vallée Poussin and Sylvain Lévi (~1921–1923). He served as Director of the Mithila Institute (~1954–1958) and General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI (~1961–1972).

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Venice, Padua, Antonianum, and the University of Chicago (PhD 2022), he held postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Tokyo (2022–2023) and Ghent University (2023).

Parimal G. Patil is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002), he was appointed Professor at Harvard University around 2004.

Parul Dave-Mukherji is an Indologist and art historian. She completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University from 2006 to 2026.

Pascale Haag (b. 1965) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle (PhD ~2002) and Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre (PhD 2018). She joined the EHESS as Associate Professor in 2003.

Pascale Hugon is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a Professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Bristol, the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012), and the Max Planck Society as Senior Research Fellow (2016).

Patricia Berger is a specialist in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman. She served as Curator at the Asian Art Museum and Professor Emerita at UC Berkeley.
